title: Slow Burn Thrillers
intro: The dread builds slowly here, like pressure behind your eyes. These are films that stay with you long after the credits roll.

films.title: Zodiac
films.line: An obsession quietly devours a man from the inside out over decades.

films.title: Prisoners
films.line: Desperation and moral rot seep into every frame like a cold November rain.

films.title: A Simple Plan
films.line: One frozen field, one terrible decision, and a friendship slowly coming undone.

films.title: Cure
films.line: Something nameless and contagious moves through a city and you feel it spreading.

films.title: The Wailing
films.line: A village unravels under a creeping dread that no one can name or outrun.

films.title: Hereditary
films.line: Grief becomes a living thing that stalks every corner of a family home.

films.title: No Country for Old Men
films.blurb: The Coens shot only 250,000 feet of film where a production this size burns 700,000, and it shows: nothing is wasted, least of all mercy. Josh Brolin's welder finds a case of drug money in the West Texas desert, and Javier Bardem's Anton Chigurh comes for it with a coin and a cattle gun. It won four Academy Awards including Best Picture, and it still refuses to give you the showdown you are waiting for.

films.title: The Vanishing
films.line: The search for an answer becomes more terrifying than the question itself.
